arxiv-1901-08159.title: Meta-Learning for Contextual Bandit Exploration
arxiv-1901-08159.creator: Amr Sharaf, Hal Daumé III
arxiv-1901-08159.description: Abstract We describe Mêlée , a meta-learning algorithm for learning a good exploration policy in the interactive contextual bandit setting. Here, an algorithm must take actions based on contexts, and learn based only on a reward signal from the action taken, thereby generating an exploration/exploitation trade-off.

arxiv-1908-06310.title: Quasirandom quantum channels
arxiv-1908-06310.creator: Tom Bannink, Jop Briët, Farrokh Labib, Hans Maassen
arxiv-1908-06310.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Tom Bannink, Jop Briët, Farrokh Labib, Hans Maassen. Mixing (or quasirandom) properties of the natural transition matrix associated to a graph can be quantified by its distance to the complete graph. Different mixing properties correspond to different norms to measure this distance. For dense graphs, two such properties known as spectral expansion and uniformity were shown to be equivalent in seminal 1989 work of Chung, Graham and Wilson.

arxiv-2002-00286.title: Families of monotone Lagrangians in Brieskorn–Pham hypersurfaces
arxiv-2002-00286.creator: Ailsa Keating
arxiv-2002-00286.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Ailsa Keating. We present techniques, inspired by monodromy considerations, for constructing compact monotone Lagrangians in certain affine hypersurfaces, chiefly of Brieskorn–Pham type. We focus on dimensions 2 and 3, though the constructions generalise to higher ones. The techniques give significant latitude in controlling the homology class, Maslov class and monotonicity constant of the Lagrangian, and a range of possible diffeomorphism types; they are also explicit enough to be amenable to calculations of pseudo-holomorphic curve invariants.

arxiv-2011-08259.description: Abstract . We prove that after inverting the Planck constant h h the Bezrukavnikov-Kaledin quantization ( X , 𝒪 h ) (X,{\mathcal{O}}_{h}) of symplectic variety X X in characteristic p p is Morita equivalent to a certain central reduction of the algebra of differential operators on X X . 1. arxiv-2203-05439.title: Spectral form factor in a minimal bosonic model of many-body quantum chaos
arxiv-2203-05439.creator: Dibyendu Roy 1 , Divij Mishra 2 and Toma z ˇ \check{\rm z} Prosen 3
arxiv-2203-05439.description: Abstract We study spectral form factor in periodically-kicked bosonic chains. We consider a family of models where a Hamiltonian with the terms diagonal in the Fock space basis, including random chemical potentials and pair-wise interactions, is kicked periodically by another Hamiltonian with nearest-neighbor hopping and pairing terms.

arxiv-2208-07962.title: Rigidity results for Riemann solitons
arxiv-2208-07962.creator: Willian Tokura, Marcelo Barboza, Elismar Batista, Ilton Menezes
arxiv-2208-07962.description: Abstract In this paper we take a look at conditions that make a Riemann soliton trivial, compacity being one of them. We also show that the behaviour at infinity of the gradient field of a non-compact gradient Riemann soliton might cause the soliton to be an Einstein manifold.

arxiv-2211-08639.title: Hierarchical Dynamic Image Harmonization DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Preprint Version 251
arxiv-2211-08639.creator: Haoxing Chen, Zhangxuan Gu, Yaohui Li, Jun Lan, Changhua Meng, Weiqiang Wang, Huaxiong Li
arxiv-2211-08639.description: Abstract . Image harmonization is a critical task in computer vision, which aims to adjust the foreground to make it compatible with the background. Recent works mainly focus on using global transformations (i.e., normalization and color curve rendering) to achieve visual consistency.

arxiv-2212-08760.title: Strong asymptotic behavior of multi-orthogonal polynomials associated with a queueing model
arxiv-2212-08760.creator: U. Fidalgo
arxiv-2212-08760.description: Abstract . We describe the strong asymptotic behavior of type I and type II multiple orthogonal polynomials which were used to give an integral expression for a transition probability function corresponding to a queueing models that has a bulk service admitting batches with a fixed size of m ∈ ℕ m\in\mathbb{N} customers.

arxiv-2404-03102.description: Abstract Despite their high relative abundance in our Universe, neutrinos are the least understood fundamental particles of nature. They also provide a unique system to study quantum coherence and the wavelike nature of particles in fundamental systems due to their extremely weak interaction probabilities.

arxiv-2406-03135.title: Very-long-baseline interferometry study of the flaring blazar TXS 1508+572 in the early Universe
arxiv-2406-03135.creator: P. Benke, A. Gokus, M. Lisakov, L. I. Gurvits, F. Eppel, J. Heßdörfer, M. Kadler, Y. Y. Kovalev, E. Ros, F. Rösch
arxiv-2406-03135.description: Abstract Context. High-redshift blazars provide valuable input to studies of the evolution of active galactic nuclei (AGN) jets and provide constraints on cosmological models. Detections at high energies ( 0.1 < E < 100 0.1<\mathrm{E}<100 GeV) of these distant sources are rare, but when they exhibit bright gamma-ray flares, we are able to study them.

arxiv-2601-10633.title: Molecularly Thin Polyaramid Nanomechanical Resonators
arxiv-2601-10633.creator: Hagen Gress, Cody L. Ritt, Inal Shomakhov, Kaan Altmisdort, Michelle Quien, Zitang Wei, John R. Lawall, Narasimha Boddeti, Michael S. Strano, J. Scott Bunch, Kamil L. Ekinci
arxiv-2601-10633.description: Abstract Abstract: Two-dimensional polyaramids exhibit strong hydrogen bonding to create molecularly thin nanosheets analogous to graphene. Here, we report the first nanomechanical resonators made out of a two-dimensional polyaramid, 2DPA-1, with thicknesses as small as 8 nm. To fabricate these molecular-scale resonators, we transferred nanofilms of 2DPA-1 onto chips with previously-etched arrays of circular microwells.

pmc-10659756.description: ObjectiveSystemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) patients are at risk during the COVID‐19 pandemic, yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. pmc-12425944.creator: Skye L. Goetz, Amy K. Glen, Gwênlyn Glusman
pmc-12425944.description: The microbiome represents a complex community of trillions of microorganisms residing in various body parts and plays critical roles in maintaining host health and wellbeing. pmc-12472298.creator: Daan van Rooij, Yuchan Mou, Tonya White, Trudy Voortman, Pauline W Jansen, Jan K Buitelaar, Bruce W Hollis
pmc-12472298.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background/Objectives: Maternal vitamin supplementation (including folic acid, vitamin D, and multivitamin supplements) during pregnancy may lower the likelihood of neurodevelopmental disorders in offspring. This study examines the associations between maternal vitamin suppletion during pregnancy and morphological patterns in offsprings’ brain structure and traits of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and Attention-Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in a large population-based study of child development.

pmc-12605108.creator: Yiqi Song, Zhenpeng Li, Xiaotong Zhu, Guang Pei, Juanyi Hou, Shiji Liu, Yi Xie, Yongtao Xie
pmc-12605108.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ObjectiveChildren’s motor development is closely related to the development of their brain functions. This study investigated the changes of EEG patterns in DCD boys.MethodsIn this study, 15 boys with DCD were screened via the Movement Assessment Battery for Children 2nd Edition (MABC-2), and 15 boys with typical development (TD) at the same age were matched as the control group.

pmc-12647704.title: Reduced Fc-mediated antibody responses after COVID-19 mRNA vaccination in a cohort of people living with HIV-1
pmc-12647704.creator: Jéromine Klingler, Priyanka Gadam Rao, Juan C Bandres, Ismael Pena, Katherine Bolanos Roldan, Gagandeep Singh, Brian Monahan, Charles Gleason, Yuexing Chen, Stefan Slamanig, Weina Sun, Chitra Upadhyay, Catarina E Hioe
pmc-12647704.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). HIV-1 infection has been associated with increased COVID-19-related hospitalization and greater SARS-CoV-2 shedding. People living with HIV-1 (PLWH) also have higher risks to other respiratory infections and lower response rates to influenza and pneumococcal vaccines, even after antiretroviral therapy. This observational study evaluated serum antibody responses after mRNA COVID-19 vaccination in elderly male cohorts of PLWH on antiretroviral therapy and people without HIV-1 (PWOH). Specifically we measured the titers, isotypes/subtypes, and functions of antibodies after the third dose of mRNA COVID-19 vaccines.

pmc-12823652.description: Microbially induced carbonate precipitation (MICP) has proven to be an effective method for soil reinforcement. pmc-13602034.title: Orthoplastic limb salvage in 12 days: Integrated reconstruction of a severe open tibial fracture
pmc-13602034.creator: Roberto Herrera, Agustin Davies, Jesica Presas, Mariano Codesido, Macarena Otero
pmc-13602034.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This case illustrates how coordinated orthoplastic management integrating staged biological optimization, definitive skeletal stabilization, and microsurgical reconstruction may improve outcomes in devastating lower-extremity trauma while reducing delays, complications, and reconstructive burden.Keywords: Open tibial fracture, Orthoplastic surgery, Limb salvage, Free flap reconstruction, Intramedullary fixation, Gustilo IIIB

Introduction

Severe Gustilo-Anderson type IIIB open tibial fractures remain among the most challenging injuries in orthopaedic trauma because successful limb salvage requires simultaneous management of skeletal instability, extensive soft-tissue loss, contamination, and infection risk.
